item.title: Ex-BYU football star Curtis Brown, family grieving after 2-year-old son died in drowning accident
item.description: A GoFundMe campaign has raised over $77,000 after former BYU football player Curtis Brown's 2-year-old son Haze drowned in a pool in Clovis, California.
item.content:encoded:
Former BYU Cougars football player Curtis Brown and his family, including his wife Kim, are grieving after a drowning accident led to the death of their 2-year-old son, Haze.

Haze drowned in the pool at the Brown family home in Clovis, California, July 26, police told the New York Post.

A GoFundMe page was started by Chandler Pearson, a family friend who wrote on the site that the Brown family is dealing with an "unimaginable loss."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"Kim and Curtis recently lost their miracle baby, Haze, in a tragic drowning accident. No words can ease the heartbreak they are facing as they grieve the loss of their precious son," Pearson wrote on the GoFundMe page.

"Many of you know and love Kim, Curtis, and their family, and have reached out asking how you can support them during this incredibly difficult time. One meaningful way to help is by contributing to this GoFundMe campaign. Your donation will help ease the financial burden of funeral expenses and other unexpected costs, allowing the Brown family to focus on healing and being together.

"Every act of kindness, no matter the size, reminds them that they are surrounded by a community that loves them deeply. Thank you for your generosity, compassion, and support during this heartbreaking time."

OLE MISS FILES LAWSUITS AGAINST COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYERS WHO LEFT FOR LANE KIFFIN'S LSU

The New York Post added that a family member found Haze unresponsive in the pool and immediately called 911, and police, EMTs and firefighters responded.

CPR was attempted on the toddler, but it was unsuccessful. Haze was taken to a nearby hospital and was later declared dead.

The GoFundMe page had received $77,375 in donations at the time of writing.

"It’s an extremely unfortunate situation," Clovis Police Department spokesman Ty Wood told the New York Post. "Adults should never let children swim unsupervised and should always learn CPR and keep rescue equipment nearby."

Brown and his wife are the parents of five, including son Trey and triplets Cruze, Julie and Kash.

Brown played five seasons with the Cougars from 2002 to 2006, including a redshirt sophomore campaign in 2003. He came into his own in 2004, racking up 789 yards on 158 carries with six touchdowns and cementing himself as someone to lead the way for BYU the next season.

Brown did just that, leading the Mountain West Conference with 14 rushing touchdowns, while registering 1,123 yards on 210 carries. He also had 454 receiving yards on 53 receptions with two more scores through the air.

In his final year, Brown had 1,010 yards on the ground and 566 through the air with 10 total touchdowns over 13 games.

Brown finished his BYU career with 3,241 rushing yards and 1,309 receiving yards with 36 touchdowns over 52 games. He owned the rushing record in school history before Harvey Unga broke it in 2009.

Brown looked to the NFL as his next step in 2007, signing with the Cincinnati Bengals as an undrafted free agent. However, after four appearances during the preseason, the Bengals released him before Week 1.

BYU didn't immediately respond to a request for comment by Fox News Digital.

item.title: Ted Cruz demands Fauci face jail time, labels him America's 'most damaging bureaucrat'
item.description: Ted Cruz says Anthony Fauci should face contempt charges, perjury prosecution and jail after pleading the Fifth over 100 times at a Senate hearing.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, is calling for Anthony Fauci to be held in contempt, prosecuted for perjury and sent to jail after the former White House COVID-19 advisor pleaded his Fifth Amendment right more than 100 times during a Senate hearing Wednesday.

"Years from now, they'll look back and say, ‘What collective madness overtook this country?’" Cruz told Fox News Digital.

"I think Anthony Fauci has had contempt for Congress and contempt for the American people for decades," he said. "His diary shows that he deliberately lied to the American people over and over and over again."

FAUCI PLEADS FIFTH WITH 'ZERO LEGAL JUSTIFICATION' AS CRITICS ERUPT AND DEMAND CONTEMPT CHARGES

Cruz made the comments after Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee Chairman Rand Paul announced he will seek contempt charges against Fauci after Fauci dodged self-incrimination by refusing to answer any questions throughout the entirety of the hearing.

"Dr. Fauci ought to think about what it says about the end of his career, that what he will be remembered for the most is pleading the Fifth more than 100 times," Cruz said.

"He's been the most damaging bureaucrat in the history of America."

RAND PAUL SEEKS CONTEMPT CHARGES AFTER FAUCI INVOKES FIFTH AMENDMENT MORE THAN 100 TIMES

Cruz and Fauci have had a longstanding feud, similar to his relationships with other GOP senators like Paul, over Fauci’s handling of the outbreak and claims he was dishonest about the origins of COVID-19 to both Congress and the American people.

"In his diary, he wrote early on that it was clear that the COVID virus did not come from the wet market in Wuhan, and then he turned around and said exactly the opposite thing on national television," Cruz said.

The released private diaries expose that Fauci considered possibilities about how the virus originated that he later downplayed to the public. He wrote that scientists considered the possibility of a deliberately inserted laboratory origin worthy of further expert review, while his later statements suggested the opposite to the public.

LEGACY MEDIA IGNORES MASSIVE ANTHONY FAUCI DOCUMENT RELEASE ALLEGING HE MISLED CONGRESS ON COVID ORIGINS

The Texas senator also accused Fauci of pushing for the lockdown of schools. Fauci wrote in his diary that he convinced both New York and California government officials to lock down their state’s school systems. This was, again, contradictory to what he said publicly, when he claimed multiple times in interviews and testified to the House Oversight Committee that he "did not close the schools."

"In his diary, he brags about convincing Democrats in New York and California to shut schools down, and yet he goes on TV and says, ‘Oh, I wasn't for shutdowns,’" Cruz said.

"The school shutdowns, which Fauci bragged that he was responsible for, may well be the single most destructive public policy step we've seen in decades. That learning loss will stick with those kids the rest of their lives when they're 90 years old.

"They will still be suffering the consequences of Anthony Fauci's corrupt and dishonest shutdowns.

"The fact that he knew he was lying to the American people — he should be held in contempt, he should be prosecuted for perjury, and he should go to jail."

item.title: Frozen pizza brand celebrates 50 years by throwing every topping you can think of on a pie
item.description: Red Baron celebrates 50 years of frozen pizza by offering winners a pie loaded with 50 toppings, pushing the limits of what belongs on a slice.
item.content:encoded:
Frozen pizzas have been a staple of freezers for decades, a useful option for a late-night snack or a contingency plan when you mess up the better dinner you were trying to cook.

And, for 50 years, one of the biggest players in the game has been Red Baron.

Now, the pizza brand is celebrating its 50th anniversary by dumping just about anything you can think of on top of a pie.

REDS FANS GO BERSERK AFTER CATCHER TYLER STEPHENSON'S ABS CHALLENGE WINS THEM FREE PIZZA

That's right, they're giving lucky winners the chance to go to town on a pizza with 50 toppings.

Baron von Richthofen himself could never have imagined when he was shot down during the Fourth Battle of Ypres that this would be his legacy...

You can enter to win one on the company's website, but I don't even think I could name fifty pizza toppings. If someone locked me in a room and said I couldn't come out until I did, I'd probably get about 25 before I started panicking.

KFC PLANS TO TEST A NEW PROTOTYPE CALLED OPEN HOUSE

I'd get to arugula, and then I'd be like, "Sh--; someone has to have put rhubarb on pizza, right? RIGHT?!"

A lot is happening on that pie, maybe too much.

I don't usually go too far beyond sausage, pepper, and onion on my bespoke pies, and I'm not averse to keeping it au naturel and going plain.

But I'm open to experimentation on the pizza front and would be open to popping this into the ol' General Electric oven and seeing what it's all about.

Hell, I went on a cruise earlier this year, and they had grape and gorgonzola pizza. I thought that broke some laws (good thing we were in international waters at the time), and it turned out to be one of the best pizzas I've ever had.

Certainly not a daily driver like a nice Hot-N-Ready or a pie from the mom & pop joint down the street. But if you want to put the top down and let your hair blow in the wind, that's when you bust out a flashy pizza like a grape and gorgonzola or, in this case, everything they had on hand at the Red Baron plant.
